approach: Add `check_root_cause_criterion(reading, request, attempt)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs after `check_code_survey`, with one `step!(check_root_cause_criterion(reading, request, attempt));` line after `step!(check_code_survey(reading));` in `refusing_check` (3138). It applies when the reading has a capability and no question, the class is `code` or `tests`, at least one criterion is Behavior (the `check_code_survey` precondition), and the request text, plus the retried job's request when `attempt` is set, is a wrong-output report. Round 4 changes: (1) the cue text is the request plus `attempt.request`, so `athena retry` (request `try again on <id>`, reading.rs:1119) is guarded; (2) the wanted-content family is narrowed so feature changes such as `Make the status page show only running jobs` are not caught; (3) steward template lines are removed only when the text also has the `Fix the root cause of a repeated failure:` title line. When the check applies, the reading needs (a) a criterion with `root cause`, a location token and a reason word, and (b) one Behavior criterion naming a test, a real-data word and a failure on the base. The error names each missing part with fixed phrases. Unit tests, corpus cases (including a retry case), one READING_RULES line and one CHANGELOG entry follow. The reader prompt, pipeline, records and athena-cli are not touched.

decisions.choice: Fix at the reading gate as a new `step!` in `refusing_check`, taking the same `attempt` argument that `check_prior_result_and_scope` side uses.
decisions.reason: Both jobs were accepted because the gate required no diagnosis. The gate runs on every reading with no model call, and `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` forces a refusing case. The reader prompt has 3 tokens of headroom (docs/system-facts.md, budget reader 1997 of 2000) and is out of scope.

rejected.why: Out of scope, no headroom, not enforced.
One instance of the class; dropped by the brief.

rejected.option: Run new tests on a scratch copy of the base in the pipeline
rejected.why: A pipeline change, left for a separate job; this job requires only that a criterion say the test fails on the base.

decisions.choice: Read the cue text from `request` and from `attempt.map(|a| a.request.as_str())`, after removing steward template lines from each text. Do not read `referenced`.
decisions.reason: Finding 1. A retry's request is `try again on <id>` (RETRY_PREFIX, reading.rs:1119, 1310), and the bug report is only in `attempt.request` (EarlierAttempt, passed through `refusing_check` at 3119-3125 and from the gate call at reading.rs:663). The class recurred across t4qv then 3gkq, a retry, so reading `request` alone leaves one of the two ways in unguarded. `referenced` holds cited evidence jobs, not the job being fixed, so it is not read. `check_reading_text` passes `None`, so the CLI check reads the request only.

rejected.why: Returns Ok for every `athena retry` of a bug-fix job.
Cited evidence jobs are not the job being fixed; it would refuse unrelated work.

decisions.choice: Decide applicability from request text with three cue families, no mandatory `Bug fix:` declaration. (i) error words: whole word wrong, incorrect, incorrectly, stale, broken, bug, bugs, regression. (ii) fix, fixes, fixed or fixing with an output noun (page, output, report, listing, table, view, dashboard, site) on the same line. (iii) wanted content, narrowed in round 4: a content verb (list, lists, show, shows, display, displays, include, includes, contain, contains, publish, publishes) with an output noun (not output or report) on a line that either has a strong restrictor (still, anymore, the phrase no longer) or has `only` and either starts with the content verb (after any bullet marker) or holds the word now; and the line has no creation word (add, adds, create, creates, new, introduce, implement) and no change word (make, makes, change, changes, redesign, rename, refactor, migrate).
decisions.reason: Finding 2 and the earlier finding that the class is defined by requests that described wanted page content: HISTORY.txt:13 'Show only open, above-limit proposals on the decisions page'; CHANGELOG.md:375 'now lists only proposals that wait for the owner'; CHANGELOG.md:384 'no longer lists proposals that were approved or rejected'. Each of these is matched (imperative `Show only`, `now lists only`, `no longer lists`). A bare `only` in the middle of a sentence, as in `Make the status page show only running jobs`, is a feature change and is not matched; the change-word list also exempts `Redesign the dashboard so it still shows the cost column`. Known gap, stated in the doc comment: a bug request worded `The page should list only X` is not caught by (iii); an error word or `fix` still catches it.

rejected.option: Mandatory `Bug fix: yes|no` assumption modelled on `Code survey:`
rejected.why: No stored reading has the line, so the replay (REPLAY_HOLD_PERCENT 10, reading.rs:3630) would count nearly every past code reading with a Behavior criterion as newly refused. An optional line adds no enforcement.
Returns Ok for the wanted-content shape of the cited jobs.

rejected.option: Bare `only` anywhere on a line as a cue
rejected.why: Catches `Make the status page show only running jobs` and forces the reader to invent a root cause.

rejected.option: Bare words fix and failure as cues
rejected.why: Catches CI races, prompt gaps and every steward job.
`fixture` and `prefix` contain `fix`.

decisions.choice: Remove steward template lines (lines starting `Failure class:`, `Cause:`, `Seen ` or `Introspection `, and the title line `Fix the root cause of a repeated failure:`) from a text only when that text also has a line starting `Fix the root cause of a repeated failure:`. Apply it to the request and to `attempt.request` separately.
decisions.reason: Finding 4. hestia.rs:406-434 builds every steward request from that title line plus those lines; a user request that happens to start a line with `Introspection ` must keep that line for cue matching. The title line is the marker that the text is a steward template.

rejected.option: Drop those prefixes from every text
rejected.why: Hides cues in user requests that start a line with `Introspection `.
The bare words fix and failure in the title would match every steward job.

decisions.choice: The root-cause criterion must contain `root cause` (a hyphen read as a space), a location token and the whole word because, why or since. A location token is `::`, `.rs`, `()`, an `_` with a letter on each side, or a `/` token with two or more slashes or a `.` extension. The doc comment says this is a text floor and the verifier and critic judge the diagnosis.
decisions.reason: Earlier signal words let `states the root cause and why it happened` pass with no named entry point. A location token forces the reader to name the file or function where wrong items enter. The copied steward bullet `The root cause is named in the change description and fixed where it originates` has no location token and no reason word, so no copy-removal helper is needed.

rejected.why: A copied request bullet satisfies it.
Passes with no named location.
Fits only the filter bug of the decisions page.

decisions.choice: The test criterion is one Behavior criterion with a whole word test or tests, a data word (real, recorded, decided, stored, actual, captured, or a word starting reproduc), a word starting `fail` and the whole word `base`.
decisions.reason: Introspection 20261105-051344-q9fv records tests that also pass on the base. Naming the base-failing run in one criterion is the reading-level part in scope. `reproduc*` lets a bug with no stored data say how it is reproduced. One criterion stops the parts being spread over several.

rejected.option: Test word and data word only
rejected.why: Does not require a failure on the base.
A bug with no stored data could not pass.

decisions.choice: Require a Behavior criterion before the check applies, as `check_code_survey` does (reading.rs:3453).
decisions.reason: The fake reader gives class `code` (crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs:278) and one content criterion (fake.rs:285), so athena-cli tests that drain fake readings are untouched. The cost is that a bug-fix reading with only content criteria is exempt, the same gap as the code survey; the doc comment states it.

rejected.why: Reaches fake readings in athena-cli tests.

decisions.choice: Add a seventh `READING_RULES` line in briefs.rs naming `check_root_cause_criterion`, and update the test that counts the rules and its stale 'six rule lines' comment (briefs.rs ~3983).
decisions.reason: The reader should hear the rule before it is refused. READING_RULES is a section of the reader brief (briefs.rs:2121-2122), outside the always-loaded reader prompt set. briefs.rs is a listed deliverable.

rejected.why: Every bug-fix reading would be refused once and read again.

decisions.choice: Cover the one-line CLI output through `check_reading_text` in a reading.rs unit test, and do not edit crates/athena-cli.
decisions.reason: `check_reading_command` (athena-cli main.rs:526-554) returns the `check_reading_text(..)` line, which collapses white space (reading.rs:3671-3682). The existing main.rs tests cover printing and exit code 2.

rejected.why: Not a listed deliverable and adds no coverage beyond `check_reading_text`.

decisions.choice: If the replay of past readings holds the job (more than REPLAY_HOLD_PERCENT 10 of up to 50 newly refused), the producer and verifier report the share and do not widen the exemptions or loosen the check to get under 10%.
decisions.reason: Finding 3. The accepted reading's own estimate (12%) is above the hold, and it sits in an assumption, which `replay_declaration` (reading.rs:3880, reads only criteria and out_of_scope) does not read. The user said the higher rate is intended; loosening would undo the fix.

rejected.option: Narrow the cues until the replay passes
rejected.why: Defeats the intended coverage and hides the cost the user accepted.

It returns Ok when capability is None, a question is set, the class is not `code` or `tests`, no criterion is Behavior, or no cue is found in the request or the attempt's request.

Helpers. `report_lines(text)`: if some line starts `Fix the root cause of a repeated failure:`, drop that line and every line starting `Failure class:`, `Cause:`, `Seen ` or `Introspection `; otherwise keep every line; return lines lowercased with leading bullet markers (`-`, `*`, `N.`, `N)`) trimmed. `is_wrong_output_report(lines)` is true when some line has (i) a whole word wrong, incorrect, incorrectly, stale, broken, bug, bugs or regression; (ii) a whole word fix, fixes, fixed or fixing and a whole output noun (page, output, report, listing, table, view, dashboard, site); or (iii) a content verb (list, lists, show, shows, display, displays, include, includes, contain, contains, publish, publishes), an output noun other than output and report, a restrictor (a strong one: the word still or anymore, or the phrase no longer; or the word only when the line starts with a content verb or holds the word now), no creation word (add, adds, create, creates, new, introduce, implement) and no change word (make, makes, change, changes, redesign, rename, refactor, migrate). Use `has_phrase` for whole words. The cue text is `report_lines(request)` plus `report_lines(attempt.request)` when attempt is Some; `referenced` is not read.

`is_root_cause_criterion(text)` reads the normalised text with hyphens as spaces. It needs the phrase `root cause`, a location token (`::`, `.rs`, `()`, an `_` with a letter on each side, or a `/` token with two or more slashes or a `.`), and the whole word because, why or since. `is_base_failing_test_criterion(c)` needs kind Behavior, a whole word test or tests, a data word (real, recorded, decided, stored, actual, captured, reproduc*) and a `fail` word plus the whole word `base`. Bail with `the reading was refused because ...`, listing only the missing parts with the fixed phrases `a criterion that names the root cause (where wrong items enter and why they are not excluded)` and `a criterion for a test built from real decided data that fails on the base`, and say what to write (name the file or function and a reason; say the test fails on the base tree).

Doc comment of the function: root cause (bug-fix readings were accepted with no diagnosis and no base-failing real-data test); jobs 20261103-201526-t4qv and 20261103-231808-3gkq; introspections 20261104-054700-e6js and 20261105-051344-q9fv; when it applies (request and retried attempt's request; steward template lines; Behavior precondition; creation and change words); known gaps (content-only readings, `should list only`, steward requests); that it is a text floor and the verifier judges the diagnosis; and the sentence `This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.` Do not write the string `pub fn check_root_cause_criterion` anywhere before the definition, because the doc test splits on its first occurrence.

risks.risk: The replay of past readings may newly refuse more than 10% (estimate, not measured), and the reading's own 12% estimate is above the hold.

If the replay holds the job, the producer and verifier report the share and do not widen exemptions to get under 10%; open question 1 flags the missing declaration.

risks.risk: A false refusal on a feature or process request that has a cue for another reason (a `stale lock file`, `still shows` on a page the request changes).
risks.mitigation: The cue lists are short and whole-word; creation and change words exempt feature shapes. The error says exactly what to write. Corpus accept cases cover `fixture`, `prefix`, `retry on failure`, `Fix the directory crash`, `Add a page that shows only failed jobs`, `Make the status page show only running jobs` and `Redesign the dashboard so it still shows the cost column`.

risks.risk: A bug request worded `The page should list only X` (no error word, no fix, no `now`) is not caught by family (iii).

risks.risk: A bug-fix reading with only content criteria skips the check.
risks.mitigation: Same gap as `check_code_survey`; stated in the doc comment. The criteria-evidence rule and the new reader rule line push toward Behavior criteria. Closing it is a separate job.

risks.risk: Steward root-cause requests are exempt because their template lines are removed before cues are matched, and a retry of a steward job reads the attempt's request with the same removal.
risks.mitigation: Those requests already carry the root-cause bullet; the gate targets user requests. Stated in the doc comment.

risks.risk: The location-token test is too strict or too loose for a real diagnosis.
risks.mitigation: Declared a text floor. The accept unit test covers a path-only location, a `()` token, an `::` token and an `_` identifier, and the error shows examples to write.
